newsitem.title: USA: WASHINGTON WHEAT, BARLEY YIELDS REPORTED VERY GOOD.
newsitem.headline: WASHINGTON WHEAT, BARLEY YIELDS REPORTED VERY GOOD.

text.p: The following is the weekly crop update from the Washington Agricultural Statistics Service for the week ended Sunday, August 10.
WEEK IN BRIEF: Warm, dry conditions continue.
Fruit growers irrigate at full capacity.
Very good wheat and barley yields reported.

Days suitable for fieldwork averaged 7.0. Topsoil moisture was 40 percent short, and 60 percent adequate. Subsoil moisture was 30 percent short, and 70 percent adequate. Irrigation water supplies were 100 percent adequate. Wheat harvest continued under warm, sunny conditions. Reported wheat and barley yields have been very good across harvested areas to date. Some lower rainfall areas continued to report near record yields. Dry pea harvest progressed well, with mixed yields reported.

Central Washington reported that the hot weather has done little damage to fruit with growers irrigating at full capacity to maintain crops. Warm weather advanced maturity and some early apple harvest was expected to start over the next couple of weeks. Bartlett pear harvest began, peach harvest progressed well, and blueberry harvest continued. Tomatoes suffered from late blight in some areas and potato vines were removed to prevent the spread of disease. Truck farmers reported excellent sales of early produce.

Range and pasture conditions were reported as 7 percent very poor, 10 percent poor, 18 percent fair, 60 percent good, and 5 percent excellent. Grazing land began to show the effects of the hot, dry conditions, with some pastures drying up and turning brown. Hay and other roughage supplies were 10 percent short, 75 percent adequate, and 15 percent surplus. Second cutting of alfalfa neared completion whereas the second cutting of timothy hay in central Washington remained two to three weeks away.

High pressure dominated Washington state with above normal temperatures and generally dry conditions. Temperatures ranged from 2 to 3 degrees above normal in the west, to 5 to 9 degrees above normal in the east. Precipitation was minimal and was limited to a few thunderstorms, mainly over the mountainous areas and the central part of the state.

Grays Harbor: Very warm temperatures and dry conditions kept agricultural producers busy irrigating. Dry pea harvest is approximately 60 percent complete with disappointing yields. Pastures have quickly turned brown. Blueberry harvest was in full swing.

Lewis: Wheat harvest was wrapping up and straw baling continued. Silage corn did well in the hot, dry weather. Blueberry harvest neared completion. Garlic was harvested. Tomatoes suffered from late blight. Potato vines were removed to help prevent the spread of disease. Pastures grew well though growth has slowed due to the hot, dry weather.

Thurston: Ag producers continued to irrigate due to very dry, warm conditions. Turfgrass growers cultivated harvested fields in preparation for planting. Truck farmers reported excellent direct farm sales of early produce.

Chelan/Douglas/Okanogan: Some record breaking hot weather has done little damage to fruit. Growers irrigated at full capacity to maintain the crops. Irrigation water was very plentiful this season. Early apple harvest will begin on a low number of acres over the next couple of weeks. Grant: Dry bean cutting began. Sweet corn harvest continued. The Grant County fair will be from August 12 through August 16.

Kittitas: Swathing of small grains began late in the week. Most of the fall grains will be swathed, weather permitting, during the next seven days. The second cutting of timothy hay should begin in 2+ to 3 weeks. Almost all of the sweet corn was in tassel, hastened by the warm weather. Yakima: Bartlett pear harvest began in the lower valley. Ginger Gold apple harvest neared completion. Warm weather was rapidly advancing maturity. Peach harvest was going well. The cool July has kept the range conditions near ideal.
Adams: Harvest of cereal grains continued under warm, sunny conditions.

Ferry: Cutting of oat hay and alfalfa hay finished late due to earlier rain. Heavy lightning and rain was received in the central areas of the county. Garfield: Harvest continued at a rapid pace with only a few fires to date. Pend Oreille: Hot weather has been good for haying. Most haying was
way behind schedule. Grass growth was good with the good soil moisture and hot temperatures. Pastures still had a few areas of standing water.

Spokane: Grain harvest started in earnest. Lentils were being swathed. Blue grass seed harvest wound down. Whitman: Reports of wheat and barley yields have been very good for the area harvested so far. In lower rainfall areas, some growers reported near record yields. Dry pea harvest progressed well, with mixed yields reported by growers, ranging from average to excellent. Grazing lands began to show the effects of the hot, dry conditions experienced over the last couple of weeks.
